( System ) Evidence In, Coaching Out

The
Pipeline

From one game-speed frame to a decision your athlete can repeat.

Frame locked Metric traced Retry verified
( Method ) From Film To Feedback

A repeatable performance loop.
No black-box score.

Every result is linked to the original frame, sensor sample, and coaching cue. Re-run the same drill, compare the same metric, and prove what changed.

  1. 01
    Capture

    Record from a compatible phone, sideline camera, or validated high-speed combine rig.

  2. 02
    Resolve

    Map joints, ball flight, foot pressure, and court position into one time-aligned possession.

  3. 03
    Coach

    Translate raw movement into a precise correction athletes can understand and repeat.

  4. 04
    Verify

    Compare the next rep against the baseline and retain the evidence trail for staff.

01 / TRACEABLE

Every metric keeps its source frame.

Review exactly where a reading came from instead of trusting an unexplained composite score.

02 / COACH-READY

Signal first. Dashboard second.

Critical cues are readable courtside, exportable for scouting, and structured for player development.

03 / PLAYER-OWNED

Portable data without hardware lock-in.

Use standard camera feeds, retain athlete records, and move the complete history with your program.

( Field Guide ) Common Inquiries

Frequently Asked Questions

CourtSpec uses multi-view computer vision calibrated to standard court and rim geometry. A production deployment must validate camera calibration and measurement tolerance against its intended training environment.

The workflow is designed around standard camera feeds, including common streaming formats. Compatibility, latency, and security must be verified for each court before production use.

The interface uses a configurable reference range for coaching comparisons. It should support a coach's assessment rather than present one universal release angle as a guarantee for every athlete.

This static demonstration stores no athlete telemetry. A production deployment must document consent, access, retention, encryption, export, and deletion controls before making regulatory or league-compliance claims.
